description: Preswald is a WASM packager for Python-based interactive data apps: bundle full complex data workflows, particularly visualizations, into single files, runnable completely in-browser, using Pyodide, DuckDB, Pandas, and Plotly, Matplotlib, etc. Build dashboards, reports, and notebooks that run offline, load fast, and share like a document.

summary.one_liner: Preswald is a Python framework that packages interactive data apps, with UI, logic, and data, into a static, offline-capable HTML app that runs in the browser via Pyodide and DuckDB.
summary.what_it_does: Preswald lets you write data apps in Python using prebuilt UI components such as tables, charts, and forms. The `preswald export` command builds an app into a static site in `dist/` that bundles the Python code (via Pyodide), data files, and DuckDB queries. The README says the app runs offline in a modern browser and can be shared as a file folder or embedded in hosting platforms. Its reactive engine re-runs only the parts affected by a change, using a dependency DAG. For development, `preswald run` starts a local server. Apps are configured through a `preswald.toml` file that sets title, port, branding, logging, and entrypoint.
use_cases: Build analyst dashboards that can be shared as static sites
Ship a data tool to stakeholders who should not install anything
Package offline data apps for fieldwork or air-gapped environments
Create interactive reports that update based on user input
Inspect local files, logs, or snapshots with a purpose-built UI
Work with sensitive data while keeping full local control
notable: Compiles a full Python app into a single shareable HTML file or static folder that runs in the browser with no server
Reactive engine that re-runs only what depends on a changed input, powered by a dependency DAG
Built-in UI components for tables, charts, and forms
Designed so AI agents can inspect and modify app code
Project scaffolding via `preswald init` with a preswald.toml config file
caveats: The README does not state platform or browser-compatibility limits beyond 'modern browser'
Browser-side Pyodide execution may limit which Python packages and data sizes are practical; the README does not detail this
The README does not describe a paid tier or hosting service
